claim: The mandatory county auditor real property transfer (conveyance) fee is $1 or 10 cents per $100 (or fraction) of value of real property transferred, whichever is greater, with listed exemptions (e.g., transfers to confirm/correct a deed, gifts between spouses or parent and child, pursuant to court order not resulting from a sale, no-consideration transfers, transfers to a revocable trust).
The grantor (seller) pays the 319.54(G)(3) fee and any county real property transfer tax levied under ORC Chapter 322 at deed delivery, via statement of value filed with the county auditor.

A county may levy an additional (permissive) real property transfer tax not exceeding 30 cents per $100 of value; the tax is levied on and paid by the grantor to the county auditor before the deed is presented to the recorder.

Transferors of residential real property (1-4 dwelling units) by sale, land installment contract, lease with option to purchase, exchange, or 99-year renewable lease must complete the Ohio property disclosure form and deliver a signed, dated copy to the prospective transferee or agent as soon as practicable; the form is prescribed by the Director of Commerce.

Exempt transfers include court-ordered transfers, deed in lieu of foreclosure, foreclosure sales, fiduciary transfers in estate/guardianship/trust administration, co-owner transfers, transfers to spouse or lineal relatives, divorce-decree transfers, government transfers, new never-inhabited construction, transfers to a transferee who occupied as residence 1+ year, and transfers by a transferor who inherited and did not occupy within the prior year.

Transferor is not liable in damages for errors or omissions not within transferor's actual knowledge; disclosures must be made in good faith, good-faith approximations allowed; form may be amended in writing.

Buyer who receives the form (or amendment) after making an offer may rescind in writing within 3 business days of receipt, but no later than the earlier of 30 days after offer acceptance or closing; if no form is ever delivered after offer, buyer may rescind by the earlier of 30 days after acceptance or closing. Transfer is not invalidated by failure to deliver.
Form must address water supply, sewer system, structure condition, hazardous materials (lead paint, asbestos, UFFI, radon) and known material defects; the Director of Commerce prescribes it.
Dept of Commerce prescribes the Residential Property Disclosure Form by rule; rule shown effective June 1, 2022 (form 'Eff. 6/2022').

When a mortgage is foreclosed, a sale of the property shall be ordered by the court of common pleas having jurisdiction; court may order sale in parcels or as a whole.
Sheriff calls three disinterested freeholders to appraise land levied upon; for residential property they must return an estimate within 21 calendar days of the clerk's order of appraisal.
Land may not be sold for less than two-thirds of appraised value (subject to 2329.51 and 2329.52).
Notice of sheriff sale must be published once a week for at least three consecutive weeks before the sale (or start of online sale).
Court examines the sale and, if proper, within 30 days of return of the writ journalizes satisfaction and orders title transferred to purchaser (confirmation).

Debtor may redeem from a sale at any time before confirmation by depositing with the clerk the judgment amount, costs, and 8% per annum interest on purchase money; there is no post-confirmation redemption right.

County prosecuting attorney institutes foreclosure of the state's tax lien in the treasurer's name upon delivery of a delinquent land tax certificate or master list, in a court or the county board of revision (ORC 323.66); prosecuted like mortgage foreclosure; publication three consecutive weeks if by publication.

Any person entitled to redeem delinquent land may do so before filing of the entry of confirmation of sale (or before expiry of the alternative redemption period under 323.78) by tendering taxes, assessments, penalties, interest, charges and costs to the county treasurer.

'Tax certificate' under 5721.30 is a document (physical, book-entry or electronic) at the treasurer's discretion and is distinct from the delinquent land tax certificate under 5721.13; 'certificate parcel' means the delinquent land described in a tax certificate.
No auditor conveyance fee for transfers on sale for delinquent taxes or assessments, nor from a county land reutilization corporation to a third party.
Seller disclosure form not required for court-ordered transfers or foreclosure sales.
